rationale: Music rights firm with global artists could link to Grand Prix concerts; B2B business with limited brand marketing.
changed: Bertelsmann became sole owner of BMG after KKR exited in 2023

name: Charter Communications
desc: US cable operator offering Spectrum internet, mobile, TV and voice to about 57 million customers in 41 states, plus advertising.
markets: Customers in 41 US states; no overseas operations. Announced merger with Cox Communications in 2025.
rationale: Large US consumer brand and advertising arm could tie into growing US F1 audiences; no international footprint.
changed: Announced merger with Cox Communications in 2025

name: Rogers Communications
desc: Canadian telecom and media company offering wireless, internet and cable, and owning the Toronto Blue Jays, Sportsnet and Rogers Centre.
markets: Customers across Canada; sports assets include Sportsnet and a majority stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment.
rationale: Large Canadian consumer brand with sports media assets; Canadian Grand Prix gives a domestic hook but footprint is national.
changed: Took a 75% holding in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment in 2025

name: The Walt Disney Company
desc: Entertainment conglomerate with film studios, media networks such as ABC and ESPN, streaming, theme parks, cruises and consumer products.
markets: Parks, streaming and media sales across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global family brand with media, parks and licensing assets; strong audience overlap with F1's growth and fan experiences.

name: AMC Theatres
desc: World's largest movie theatre chain, operating about 900 theatres in the US and Europe, including Odeon and UCI.
markets: Theatres across the US and Europe under AMC, Odeon and UCI brands.
rationale: Cinema chain can screen F1 content and film events; consumer reach in the US and Europe suits fan activations.

name: Comcast
desc: Media and technology conglomerate owning Xfinity broadband, NBCUniversal, Sky and theme parks, and operating internet, TV and film businesses.
markets: Operates in the US, UK, Europe and Asia through Xfinity, NBCUniversal, Sky and Universal parks.
rationale: Owns Sky, a Formula 1 broadcaster, and sports media assets; huge consumer brand with an obvious F1 tie-in.
f1: Owns Sky, a Formula 1 broadcaster; CNBC, formerly a Comcast unit, is an F1 partner

name: Legendary Entertainment
desc: Film, television and media company founded in 2000 that produces and co-finances major films such as Dune and Godzilla.
markets: Films released worldwide through studio partners; ownership by Dalian Wanda Group dates from 2016.
rationale: Film studio could do F1 content tie-ins and premiere events; limited need for traditional sponsorship.
changed: Acquired by Dalian Wanda Group in 2016

name: Liberty Media
desc: US media company that owns Formula One Group, holder of Formula 1's commercial rights, plus other sports and media assets.
markets: Formula 1 stages races across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Owns Formula 1's commercial rights, so it controls the sport rather than being a sponsorship prospect.
changed: Split off Atlanta Braves Holdings in 2023
f1: Owns Formula One Group, the commercial rights holder of Formula 1

name: Nexstar Media Group
desc: Largest US local television station owner, with over 200 stations reaching about 39 percent of US households, plus NewsNation.
markets: US local television and cable audiences only; no verified overseas operations. Agreed to acquire Tegna in 2025.
rationale: US-only broadcaster with local advertisers; some interest in US F1 audience growth but limited fit.

name: United Group
desc: Multi-play telecoms and media provider in Southeast Europe, operating mobile, broadband and pay-TV services in countries including Serbia and Bulgaria.
markets: Operates in Southeast Europe, including SBB in Serbia and Vivacom in Bulgaria; controlled by BC Partners.
rationale: Regional telecom and sports TV brand with consumer reach could benefit from F1 content and hospitality.

name: Universal Music Group
desc: World's largest music company, with labels including Republic, Interscope and Capitol, a major publishing arm and a global artist business.
markets: Operations in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America; listed on Euronext Amsterdam.
rationale: Global artist roster could support F1 concerts and fan experiences; music brand with broad consumer reach.

name: CIRSA
desc: Spanish gaming group operating casinos, slot arcades, betting shops, bingo halls and online gaming in Spain, Italy, Latin America, Morocco.
markets: Venues and online gaming in Spain, Italy, Latin America and Morocco.
rationale: Madrid joins the F1 calendar in 2026 and rival gaming brands already partner; a Spanish home market adds fit.
changed: Listed on the Spanish stock exchanges in 2025

name: SESAC Music Group
desc: US performing rights organisation and music licensing company collecting royalties for songwriters, composers and publishers when their music is played.
markets: US music licensing with offices in New York and Nashville; international activity is not confirmed.
rationale: B2B rights organisation with little consumer marketing and mainly US activity; weak F1 fit overall.

name: iQiyi
desc: Online video platform in China streaming original series, films, variety shows, anime and licensed content for subscribers and advertisers.
markets: Subscribers mainly in China; overseas streaming activity exists but is not detailed here.
rationale: Large Chinese young-audience platform could suit F1 content; strong brand but mostly domestic.

name: Take-Two Interactive Software
desc: Video game publisher behind Rockstar Games, including Grand Theft Auto, and 2K titles such as NBA 2K and Borderlands.
markets: Publishes games worldwide, with Zynga mobile games acquired in 2022.
rationale: Major games publisher with young global audience and sports titles; motorsport tie-in is plausible but not obvious.

name: Create Music Group
desc: Music services company providing distribution, rights management, publishing, royalty advances and digital media services for musicians, creators and labels.
markets: US-based music services firm; international reach and any expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Creator-focused music services firm with modest brand reach; possible content tie-ins but weak F1 fit.

name: Digikala
desc: Iran's largest online retailer, selling electronics, fashion, books, home goods and groceries, with a marketplace for third-party sellers.
markets: Customers in Iran only; operates under sanctions regime limits on international business.
rationale: Iranian company in a sanctioned market; F1 partnership is very unlikely or restricted.

name: Cologix
desc: North American network-neutral data centre and interconnection operator with facilities in markets such as Columbus, Dallas, Montreal and Toronto.
markets: Facilities across US and Canadian markets serving enterprises, cloud providers and carriers.
rationale: Data centre operator selling to enterprises; AI infrastructure rivals such as CoreWeave already in F1, but North America only.

name: Yankee Global Enterprises
desc: Steinbrenner family holding company that owns the New York Yankees baseball team and holds stakes in the YES Network.
markets: Baseball team and media assets in the New York area; brand has wide US following.
rationale: Premium US sports brand with corporate hospitality; could partner on US races but no international ops.

name: Evoke PLC
desc: London-listed gambling company, formerly 888 Holdings, owning William Hill, 888 Casino and Mr Green, serving UK and European bettors.
markets: Customers mainly in the UK and Europe through William Hill, 888 and Mr Green.
rationale: Gambling peers Betway, Allwyn and FanDuel already partner F1; strong UK consumer brands.

name: Gamma
desc: Media and music company founded in 2021 by Larry Jackson, backing artists through a record label, publishing and film.
markets: Los Angeles-based; international activity and any expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Young music and media company with artist roster could host Grand Prix entertainment; early-stage budget.

name: TKO Group Holdings
desc: US sports and entertainment company owning the UFC, WWE and PBR, formed in 2023 by combining UFC and WWE.
markets: Live events and media rights in the US, Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Major live sports and entertainment owner shares F1's fan base; partnership potential via events and hospitality.
changed: Formed in 2023 through merger of UFC and WWE

name: HengTen Networks Group
desc: Hong Kong-listed holding company with investments in internet services and applications and, later, Chinese property.
markets: Based in Hong Kong with mainland China interests; wider operations not confirmed.
rationale: Holding company with limited consumer brand and unclear current operations; F1 partnership is unlikely.

name: Gray Media
desc: US broadcaster that owns and operates local television stations affiliated with CBS, NBC, ABC and Fox in over 100 markets.
markets: US local television markets only; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: US-only local broadcaster with limited brand reach; some advertiser value but little F1 fit.
changed: Renamed Gray Media from Gray Television in 2025
